demo.cliff: which phase a change belongs in
teaches: An Active Effect lives on the Item that transfers it, and transfer: true is what carries it to whoever holds the Item.
A change has four parts: the key it writes, the type of write, the value, and the phase.
flags.mgt2.suspended is the referee's pause, kept apart from disabled, because an effect the player switched off and one the table is ignoring for a scene are different things.
demo.trap: The two effects below are the whole point of this document. Both add 1. The first writes a STORED accumulator and belongs in the initial phase. The second writes a DERIVED value and has to be final, because prepareDerivedData runs between the two phases and would overwrite an initial write with the number it recomputed. A change aimed at a derived value in the initial phase does not error, does not warn, and looks exactly like a broken effect. Core renders the phase as a hidden input, which is why this system ships its own effect configuration screen.

system.description: A referee's teaching aid, not a piece of equipment. It carries one change of each phase so the difference can be watched on a sheet.

effects.name: Demo — Initial phase
effects.description: A change on a stored accumulator. The initial phase is right, and the derived pass reads it afterwards.

effects.name: Demo — Final phase
effects.description: A change on a derived value. Move this one to the initial phase and it stops working, with no message anywhere.
